title: Arch- and seqlen-aware kernel autotune playbook and runtime hook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: We've seen model- and sequence-length-dependent variance in latency and cost when serving the same family of models across different GPU classes. Current static kernel selection (compile-time defaults + coarse heuristics) misses opportunities for throughput and latency improvements, and occasionally regresses on long-seqlen tails. Goal: Implement a lightweight, production-safe autotuning layer that picks the most efficient kernel implementation at request time based on model architecture fingerprint, observed seqlen distribution, and device capabilities. This ticket covers design, a runtime hook, offline profile collection, and an A/B rollout plan.
scope: In scope: (1) model/device fingerprinting format; (2) offline microbench profiler to produce per-(model-arch, device-class, seqlen-bucket) kernel rankings; (3) runtime cache keyed by fingerprint + seqlen bucket; (4) quick online sampling path for cold models; (5) safe fallback and performance regression detection. Out of scope: full cross-tenant model retraining, end-to-end compiler changes, and new kernel implementations (we consume existing kernels: flash-attn variants, tiled-gemm, fused-softmax, generic fallback).
success_criteria:
- p95 decode latency improved by >=10% on long-seqlen workloads for top 3 customer models (measured across dedicated and hosted pools)
- No customer-facing errors introduced during rollout (error rate delta <= 0.01%)
- Cost-per-token reduction >=5% for batch inference workloads in long-seqlen bucket.
- Feature gated + can be disabled per-customer/route.
approach_summary: 1) Build an offline microbench tool that runs a matrix of kernels across representative seqlen buckets (8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512) and device profiles (A100-80GB, A100-40GB, H100, T4). Output: ranked kernel list and banded performance stats. 2) Create compact fingerprint: (model_pkg_hash, arch_hint, kv_cache_layout, typical_tok_width) + device_capabilities signature. 3) At runtime, consult in-memory store: exact match -> use top kernel; miss -> run a 1s budgeted micro-sample on low-traffic worker to validate top candidate then cache; if sampling fails or times out, fall back to baseline robust kernel. 4) Maintain continuous telemetry and a comparator that runs shadowed requests to validate choices without affecting customers. 5) Provide per-route override and telemetry for canary rollouts.
data_model_and_cache_key: Fingerprint components (as strings): model_hash, model_family, attention_impl_hint, weight_layout, device_family, sm_count, memory_bandwidth_bucket, seqlen_bucket. Cache key stored as a single colon-joined string. Cache TTL: 24h for hot models, 7d for inactive models. Storage: local node memory + replicated metadata in Redis for cross-node warm starts.
heuristics_details:
- Prefer fused/flash kernels for seqlen <= 128 on devices with tensor-core support; prefer tiled-gemm for seqlen >= 256 on older devices.
- If kv cache memory pressure > 70%, prefer memory-efficient kernels even at modest latency cost.
- For causal decode loop, prioritize kernels with lower per-token overhead (smaller kernel launch time) for short prompt + high decode length.
- Use mixed-precision preference: if device supports fast fp16/amp and model quantization flag is set, bias toward quantized-friendly kernels.
- Add weight to recent online performance (EWMA with alpha=0.2) so the system adapts to drift.
safety_and_rollback:
- Feature gated at runtime (global flag + per-customer route flag).
- Canary rollout: start at 1% traffic, expand at 5%/25%/100% if p95 and error delta within thresholds.
- Automatic rollback trigger on: error rate increase >0.05% absolute OR p95 latency regression >15% for 10min window.
- All kernel switches are logged with stack trace and configuration to allow deterministic reproduction.
observability_and_metrics: Emit: chosen_kernel, fingerprint_key, seqlen_bucket, device_profile, request_latency_ms, decode_tokens, kernel_exec_ms, kernel_mem_bytes, fallback_reason. Dashboards: per-kernel p50/p95/p99, per-model traffic split, rollback events and heatmap by seqlen. Alerts: weekly drift on kernel rank order and immediate alert on rollout regression.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint construction and cache behavior. Integration tests that inject synthetic devices and models into the profiler and validate chosen kernel matches offline ranking. End-to-end load tests across seqlen buckets in staging with shadow traffic and canary. Backpressure tests to ensure sampling path does not saturate worker capacity.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy offline profiler and populate initial kernel table from CI lab (non-prod) -> QA validation. 2) Deploy runtime hook behind feature flag to staging with shadow mode. 3) Canary on a small set of internal routes (1%) for 24h and measure metrics. 4) Gradual ramp (5/25/100) with automated checks at each step. 5) Full rollout to dedicated pools after 100% hosted success.
Owners: runtime infra (Diego), profiling infra (Maya Singh), QA (Jonah Park).

- microbench profiler + runner (repo: github.com/redwood/runtime-kernel-profiler)
- runtime hook and cache implementation (PR: #TBD)
